Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Las Vegas NV
353 AM PST Thu Nov 19 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* A low pressure system will bring snow to the mountains of Inyo 
  County and southern Nevada beginning through Friday morning. 

* This low pressure system will also bring gusty southerly-to-
  southwesterly wind to the region today.

* There will be a brief reprieve from unsettled weather over the
  weekend before the next system impacts the area early next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...through Wednesday.

Early morning infrared and water vapor satellite imagery reveal 
widespread cloud cover spreading across southeastern California, 
southern Nevada, and northwestern Arizona as a winter storm begins 
to push into the area. This trough is already bringing rain showers, 
mountain snow, and gusty winds to the area. In the past 12 hours, 
SNOTEL sites in the Eastern Sierra have picked up around 10 to 15 
inches with additltzerional snow expected throughout the day. 
Expected snow totals in the Spring Mountains have increased, with 6 
to 12 inches of snow now expected for elevations between 7,000 and 
9,500 feet. As such, the Winter Weather Advisory has been upgraded 
to a Winter Storm Warning, which will run through early Friday 
morning. In addition to upgrading the Spring Mountains to a Winter 
Storm Warning, we have also issued a Winter Storm Warning for 
elevations above 6,500 feet in Esmeralda County and Central Nye 
County. 4 to 8 inches of snow are expected at Lida Summit in 
Esmeralda County, which will make for hazardous travel conditions. 
Outside of Lida Summit, snow accumulations up to 5 inches will be 
possible for elevations above 7,000 feet in Nye and Esmeralda 
counties. This Winter Storm Warning will also run through early 
Friday morning. While higher elevations are seeing snow, lower 
elevations and valleys can expect light-to-moderate rain as showers 
move through today.

Gusty southerly-to-southwesterly winds will also accompany this 
system. On Wednesday afternoon we saw gusty southerly wind pick up 
across Inyo, Esmeralda, and Central Nye counties. These winds have 
begun to decrease overnight. However, we will see another round of 
gusty winds today, this time across the Mojave Desert. 20 to 30 mph 
southerly-to-southwesterly winds with 40 to 50 mph gusts will 
pick up across the Mojave Desert, far southern Nevada, and 
northwestern Arizona later this morning. These winds will continue
through through the evening hours, decreasing overnight. Gusty 
southerly winds will make for difficult driving conditions on 
Highway 95 between Indian Springs, NV and Desert Rock-Mercury, NV 
today. Southerly crosswinds will also make for difficult driving 
conditions along I-40 through San Bernardino and Mohave counties. 

Weather across the region will calm down during the day on Friday as 
we find ourselves on the back side of the main trough axis. A 
secondary disturbance will swing through the area right behind the 
main trough, delivering a reinforcing shot of colder air to 
southeastern California, southern Nevada, and northwestern Arizona. 
As a result, temperatures on Friday and Saturday will top out around 
8 to 15 degrees cooler than normal for late November. Weak, 
transient ridging will set up across the area on Saturday, providing 
a brief reprieve from unsettled weather over the weekend. Long term 
guidance continues to show the potential for another weather system 
early next week. However, details regarding the timing and evolution 
of this system remain uncertain at this time.

&&

.AVIATION...For Harry Reid...For the 12Z Forecast Package...
A fairly active day expected with increasing winds, lowering 
ceilings, and the chance for showers. Light and variable winds 
expected through around noon, then S-SSW winds quickly increase to 
10-15 kt with higher gusts. Strongest gusts expected around and just 
after sunset upwards of 30 kt before diminishing after midnight. 
Expect elevated S-SW winds to persist into Friday morning. Ceilings 
gradually lower through the morning hours, starting out near 10 kft 
at the beginning of the period and reaching 7-8kft by late morning. 
As showers move in during the afternoon, ceilings may lower to 6 kft 
or lower within showers. Clearing should occur rather quickly after 
02z this evening with high confidence in VFR cigs thereafter. 
Improving conditions for Friday with lighter winds and VFR ceilings. 


For the rest of southern Nevada, northwest Arizona and southeast 
California...For the 12Z Forecast Package...An active period 
expected for the entire region with gusty winds, showers, and 
lowering ceilings. The worst conditions are expected in the Owens 
Valley, including KBIH, where gusty southerly winds to 30 kt, 
rainfall, and OVC ceilings between 1 and 3kft persist through this 
evening. Meanwhile, ceilings fall to the 4 to 6kft range across most 
of the Mojave Desert this afternoon as a line of showers moves 
through. Quick clearing expected on the backside of the 
precipitation this evening with VFR cigs and vis likely by tonight. 
Gusty southerly to southwesterly winds also pick up at most 
locations in the afternoon with gusts 30-35 kt at times. Expect 
elevated winds to continue into the overnight hours before 
diminishing by early Friday morning. Much quieter conditions 
expected the rest of the day on Friday. 

&&

.SPOTTER INFORMATION STATEMENT...Spotters are encouraged to report
any significant weather or impacts according to standard operating
procedures.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Stessman
AVIATION...Moore

For more forecast information...see us on our webpage:
https://weather.gov/lasvegas or follow us on Facebook and Twitter
